extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant recipients (PD/PIs), PD/PI delegates, Signing Officials (SO), Authorized Organizational Officials (AO), and grants management staff using eRA Commons to prepare and submit RPPRs and related materials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and policy guidance for preparing, validating, routing, and submitting Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPR), and associated additional materials (PRAM, FRAM, IRAM) in eRA Commons for NIH awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual-level participant data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: POLICY: Individual-level participant data on sex, race, ethnicity and age at enrollment is required in progress reports for competitive applications submitted for due dates on or after January 25, 2019 (See NIH Guide Notice NOT-OD-18-116). Inclusion data for subsequent RPPRs must be provided using the file upload option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload participant-level data using the Upload Participant Level Data Attachment button; uploaded data will populate the cells in the report. You can Download Current Participant Level Data for records or Remove Current Participant Level Data to clear records. Update individual enrollment count cells as necessary and select Save and Release Lock (or Cancel and Release Lock to leave without saving).

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned enrollment table structure and editability
rubrics_metrics.description: The planned enrollment table includes racial categories along the left side of the table and ethnic categories, divided by sex, along the top of the table. The individual enrollment count cells are editable and set to zero by default when populating a new IER. When editing an existing form, these values are pre-populated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total fields are calculated by HSS and sum rows/columns accordingly; the total values are not editable fields. Update the values in individual enrollment count cells as necessary and select Save and Release Lock (or Cancel and Release Lock to discard changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to planned enrollment require Program Officer contact
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are changes from the planned enrollment originally approved for funding, contact the program officer to discuss updating/revising the planned enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To edit the Inclusion Enrollment Report, from the Study Record(s) screen select the Edit link in the Action column of the Inclusion Enrollment Report section. See Section G – Special Reporting Requirements for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing Inclusion Enrollment Reports block submission (current FY)
rubrics_metrics.description: When inclusion monitoring is required and no IERs exist, RPPR system will NOT allow the submission of the progress report without IER(s). For the current FY it will display an error message and require that you submit a new enrollment record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For past FYs (late reports) a standard message is displayed instead of an error: 'NIH policy requires inclusion to be monitored, but no inclusion data record(s) (IERs) have been provided.' To add a record select Add New Inclusion Enrollment Report from Study Records(s) screen and create a new IER (if no study records exist, first add a study record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creating a new Inclusion Enrollment Report (IER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon a successful save of a new IER, attributes (Foreign/domestic indicator/planned comments), Planned Inclusion Data (as entered), and Cumulative Inclusion Data (as zeros) are also created; the new IER is assigned a unique IER #.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After creating a new IER, the cumulative counts start at zero and planned data are preserved. Use the unique IER # for tracking and future edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget form types and add/edit/delete behavior (H.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most awards now use the SF424 R&R budget form. However, training awards may use the SF424 and/or the PHS 398 training budget. The PHS Additional Indirect Costs budget form is available as an optional form for the Overall component of a multi-project award with multiple organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To add a budget choose an option from the drop-down and click Add Budget. Edit via the budget’s three-dot ellipsis menu and select Edit. Budget types can be deleted via the ellipsis Delete option; after deleting a form, save the RPPR before navigating away from the H.Budget tab (Save button at bottom). Contact the Grants Management Specialist with questions about the appropriate form to use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward budget types and limits (H.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subaward budget types include SF 424 Research & Related Subaward Budget form and PHS 398 Subaward Training Budget. The recipient may select up to 30 subaward budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To add a subaward budget, choose an option from the drop-down and select Add Subaward Budget. Edit or Delete using the subaward’s three-dot ellipsis icon and remember to click Save before exiting the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI and Organization Name pre-population and editability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-component awards, and for the OVERALL component of a multi-component award, the UEI automatically populates the Unique Entity Identifier and Organization Name fields of the recipient organization on the budget form, but these fields are NON-editable. For a multi-component award, the component’s UEI and organization name are prepopulated with the recipient organization’s data, but both fields are editable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To change UEI or organization name click magnifying glass icon to open Search Organization popup, enter UEI or organization name and click Search. If no matches, click Add New Organization to type UEI and name manually and Save. Selecting an organization updates both fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual calculation of budget line item F.5 when subaward budgets present
rubrics_metrics.description: NOTE: If subaward budgets are completed, the system will not calculate the budget line item F.5 for the main budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Total consortium costs for the main budget MUST be computed and entered manually into budget line item F.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check RPPR for Errors and Warnings — validation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before an RPPR is submitted to agency, an error check can be performed to verify that the report passes the business rules and system validations in place. Any user who has access to the RPPR may perform the error check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the three-dot ellipsis menu next to the Award Number and select Check for Errors (single-project) or use the component Check for Errors (multi-project). If errors or warnings exist, messages display for each failed occurrence. All errors must be corrected prior to submission; the system will prevent submission of an RPPR containing errors. Warnings do not prevent submission but should be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR error/warning checking behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: To perform an error check on the Overall or individual component of a multi-project RPPR select the Check for Errors option from the component’s three-dot ellipsis menu.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors or a warning exist for the chosen component, appropriate messages display. Select Check for Errors for other components to validate them. All errors must be corrected prior to submission; warnings do not prevent submission but should be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing RPPR — who can route and how
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports in Work in Progress (WIP) status can be routed to others for review or corrections by the current reviewer of the report. NOTE: A person who is delegated a role of PD/PI cannot route an RPPR to the next reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To route: on the RPPR Menu click three-dot ellipsis and select Route to Next Reviewer, choose reviewer from Next Reviewer dropdown, optionally enter comments. Required for PD/PI ONLY: click the checkbox that certifies statements are true (Signing Officials do not see this checkbox). Click Route to Next Reviewer to route; after routing, editor loses edit rights and status updates to Reviewer Work in Progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall RPPR — who can recall and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: RPPRs that have been routed to a reviewer can be recalled by the person who performed the routing action. The last reviewer of the report is able to recall it; however, Signing Officials at the Organization and the Contact PD/PI who are not the last reviewer can also recall the report when it is in a status of Reviewer Work in Progress. NOTE: A person who has been delegated the PD/PI role does not have the ability to recall the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recall, select Recall from the three-dot ellipsis menu (option appears only if you routed the RPPR or are an SO and RPPR is Reviewer WIP). Upon recall, status updates (e.g., PD/PI Work in Progress), an email is sent to the reviewer from whom it was recalled, routing audit history updated, and Edit RPPR / Route to Next Reviewer options reappear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting RPPR to Agency — who may submit and delegation limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed and validated RPPRs in a status of Work in Progress can be submitted to the Agency for acceptance. This act is performed by the Signing Official (SO) when the SO is the current reviewer of the report. For SNAP awards only, PD/PIs may also submit the report if they have been delegated submit authority by the SO. NOTE: A PD/PI with Progress Report authority cannot submit a non-SNAP or F RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit click three-dot ellipsis and select Submit from RPPR Menu. The Submit screen displays a certification statement; click I Agree to sign off. The RPPR is validated for system/business rules; errors must be corrected to submit. If warnings exist, you may Cancel to fix or OK to continue with submission despite warnings. On successful submission status becomes Submitted to Agency, routing history updated, and email notifications sent to PD/PI, SO and AO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification statements required at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit screen shows certification: (1) for clinical trials, certifies compliance with the NIH Policy on Dissemination of NIH-Funded Clinical Trial Information including registration in ClinicalTrials.gov within 21 days after enrollment and summary results submission within one year after completion; OR (2) certifies the awardee organization is in compliance with Notice of Award and Grants Policy Statement and verifies accuracy of all administrative, fiscal, and scientific information. Deliberate withholding, falsification, or misrepresentation could result in administrative actions and penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click the I Agree button to sign the certification prior to submission. Ensure ClinicalTrials.gov registration and results compliance where applicable, and verify all report information for accuracy before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project submission errors and warnings display rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon submission, multi-project RPPRs are validated and errors/warnings are displayed differently: the RPPR Menu displays the Overall messages followed by messages of the other components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All errors must be corrected before submission. Warnings are displayed under errors and do not prevent submission, but should be reviewed and addressed if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing RPPR PDF and draft/status behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: PD/PIs, PD/PI delegates, and reviewers can view a PDF version of an RPPR in Work in Progress (WIP) or Submitted to Agency status to see how it will be seen by the Agency. Until the RPPR is submitted to agency, the PDF report shows a status of Draft and a blank submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From RPPR Menu click three-dot ellipsis and select View RPPR as PDF to open the PDF in a separate window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing history audit fields
rubrics_metrics.description: From initiation to submission to Agency, the routing of an RPPR is captured for auditing purposes. The RPPR Routing History screen displays showing the Reviewer Name, Action Taken, Notification Sent (date and time), Date of Action, Next Reviewer Name, and Comments (when available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs, PD/PI delegates, and reviewers can view routing history for WIP or Submitted RPPRs at any time, even when not the current reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing completed RPPR in Commons (Status workflow)
rubrics_metrics.description: The completed RPPR, in PDF format, is accessible in Commons from the Status Information screen. For incrementally-funded and multi-year funded awards the progress reports display differently in Other Relevant Documents: incrementally-funded use e-Application link; multi-year awards show RPPR Year <X> <MM/DD/YYYY> links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Commons select Status > List of Applications/Awards, then select Application ID hyperlink to open Status Information and access Other Relevant Documents to open the RPPR PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Access PRAM purpose and acceptable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Access Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) feature provides a means for the recipient to enter, review, and submit information in response to the automated notification sent when an NIH or AHRQ recipient organization submits an RPPR with non-compliant publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using PRAM, recipients can upload and submit a My NCBI PDF report demonstrating that previously non-compliant papers reported on the RPPR are now compliant. Compliant papers have a status of Complete, N/A (not applicable), PMC Journal in Process, or In process at NIHMS. If unable to provide verification, recipients can upload justification for why specific publications cannot be brought into compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM initiation, upload, routing, recall, and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The PD/PI (Contact PI) or PD/PI Delegate can initiate PRAM by selecting Public Access PRAM from Status Result – List of Applications/Awards. A PD/PI can enter PRAM but can only submit it if delegated Submit Progress Report authority; otherwise only the SO can submit PRAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add files by drag-and-drop or browse; uploaded files can be downloaded or deleted. After routing PRAM select an SO as Next Reviewer and enter optional comments; PD/PI must read and agree to PD/PI Assurance statement to route. PRAM can be recalled by the person who routed it until submission. To submit, SO (or delegated PD/PI) accesses PRAM and clicks Submit, reads SO certification and selects I Agree. After submission status updated to Submitted and email notifications sent. Preview and view options available.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM purpose and PO-initiated requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Progress Report Additional Materials (FRAM) feature provides a means for recipients to enter, review, route, and submit information in response to specific request(s) by the Program Official (PO) for additional information related to the Final RPPR. When a FRAM request is made, the PI is notified via email; Final RPPR status on Closeout Status is updated to FRAM Requested and a FRAM Update link appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PI is responsible for uploading requested FRAM via the Closeout module in Commons and may view the original request from Status Information. After upload, the SO is able to submit FRAM to Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Outcomes public posting requirements and format constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Per the 1993 NIH Revitalization Act and the 21st Century Cures Act, NIH requires entities conducting NIH-defined Phase III Clinical Trials to include results of valid analyses by sex, race, and ethnicity, in addition to submission in ClinicalTrials.gov. Outcomes will be made publicly available with PD/PI name attached to the public posting in RePORTER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NIH awards the length of the Outcome statement should not exceed half a page. The Outcome statement text field is limited to 2000 characters. The summary must: be written for the general public in clear, concise, and comprehensible language; be suitable for dissemination to the general public; and not include proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets. NIH has provided Sample Project Outcomes and notices NOT-OD-17-022 and NOT-OD-17-037 for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM upload and submit behavior and editability rules
rubrics_metrics.description: To upload FRAM navigate to Closeout Status and click FRAM Update; drag-and-drop or browse files to upload. When files are uploaded, Closeout Status updates to show FRAM Uploaded. The SO is then able to submit FRAM to Agency. NOTE: After the SO submits FRAM, the FRAM Update link on Closeout Status will be replaced by the View FRAM link and updates can no longer be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit FRAM, SO clicks FRAM Update then Submit; Closeout Status will show FRAM Submitted By <SO Name>. Email notifications go to SO, PI, and PO. Commons generates a PDF containing all documents added to the FRAM request which can be accessed from Status Information. The PO may rescind approval, restoring the FRAM Update link. SOs can continue to add additional attachments even after submission to the Agency (before acceptance of the Final RPPR); subsequent documents will be appended to the stored PDF. Note: FRAM cannot be edited after submission to the Agency, except that SOs may append documents prior to Agency acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency may use Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM) to provide a means for the recipient to enter, review, route, and submit information in response to specific request(s) by the Program Official at the IC for additional information following the submission of an Interim RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRAM functions similarly to PRAM/FRAM for requested follow-up materials after Interim RPPR submission; specific steps and rules are covered in the IRAM section.
